entries.title: When cold becomes a tiger
entries.literal_meaning: Magha: the cold becomes a tiger.
entries.explanation: The tiger makes the cold feel fierce.
entries.meaning_odia: ମାଘର ଜୋର୍ ଶୀତକୁ ବାଘ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.usage_example: A chilly morning makes someone reach for another shawl. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: A vivid seasonal image, not a weather forecast.

entries.title: Where the cold is felt
entries.odia: ମାଘେ ଶୀତ, ମେଘେ ଶୀତ, ଯତ୍ର ବାତ ତତ୍ର ଶୀତ
entries.literal_meaning: Cold in Magha, cold under clouds; wherever wind, there cold.
entries.explanation: A rhythmic reply names occasions when cold is felt.
entries.meaning_odia: କେବେ ଶୀତ ଲାଗେ ବୋଲି ପଚାରିଲେ ଏହି ଛନ୍ଦମୟ ଉତ୍ତର ଦିଆଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Someone asks why the afternoon feels chilly; another replies with this saying. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary presents it as a reply. Its Sanskrit phrasing is retained; it is not a universal weather rule.
